newsitem.title: USA: New York Times sees Q1 EPS $0.47 to $0.57.
newsitem.headline: New York Times sees Q1 EPS $0.47 to $0.57.

text.p: New York Times Co said Thursday it expects first quarter earnings of $0.47 to $0.57 per share, higher than analysts' estimates.
The company said higher advertising revenues at its newspaper and broadcast properties and lower newsprint prices were behind the improved earnings.
In the prior year's first quarter, the company reported earnings of $0.33 per share. According to First Call, analysts' consensus estimates for this year's first quarter were $0.45 per share.
The quarter's results are to be released April 17.

The New York Times, which besides its flagship paper also owns the Boston Globe and 21 regional newspapers, said it expects newsprint prices to drift upward in 1997. However, it said newsprint prices are not expected to be as volatile as in the last two years.
The paper industry recently set increased prices, Times spokeswoman Nancy Nielsen said.
"The question is always whether it will hold or not," Nielsen said. "It's too early to tell."
The company said it will be difficult to compare full-year 1997 with 1996, which had increased revenue from the Summer Olympics and the presidential election.

In addition, it said it expects increased promotional expenses in 1997 from the planned introduction in September of a new New York regional edition of The Times and "a difficult circulation environment" for its newspaper group.
The company said it also expects increasing depreciation and decreasing capitalized interest expense from two new printing facilities that are to come online this year.
((-- Lisa Marie Pane, New York newsdesk 212-859-1713))
